u.0.1.28.t: Lighter and faster: quicker start, smaller projects in memory, one-pass stems, render-ahead, Ableton Link
u.0.1.28.s: On one Windows PC LYNX SHARE's window is ready in about a second (FL Studio 2026: 1.7 s), FL's Thief demo opens in 5.2 s with 345 MB of private memory (FL Studio: 12.2 s and 874 MB), a playing song is drawn at the display's rate, and mixer stems export in one pass, up to 19 times faster. Render-ahead and a lighter engine help heavy projects at small buffers with the same sound. The release also adds Ableton Link, Live's Freeze and Bounce, clip envelopes, samples dragged onto plugins, more of Live's devices, FL Studio Mobile's factory sounds from your own copy of the app, a 16-pad Sampler in the Simple workflow, and the experimental Remote Control API contributed by guike8.
u.0.1.28.n0: Faster and lighter (measured on one Windows PC): the window is ready in about 1 s (FL Studio 2026: 1.7 s), FL's Thief demo opens in 5.2 s (FL Studio: 12.2 s) and holds 345 MB of private memory (FL Studio: 874 MB), opening a big project no longer freezes the window, and a playing song is drawn at the display's rate (143 screen updates a second on a 144 Hz display; FL Studio: 143.8).
u.0.1.28.n1: Stems in one pass: one render feeds every mixer-track stem and the full mix. Thief's 27 stems went from about an hour to about three minutes.
u.0.1.28.n2: Render-ahead (Options › Audio settings, on by default): the part of a project you are not playing live is rendered about 23 ms ahead on its own thread, so heavy projects hold small buffers with less CPU and fewer dropouts.
u.0.1.28.n3: Ableton Link: tempo, beat and start / stop in sync with Live and other Link apps on your network. The Link toggle is in the Clip-launch toolbar, and in Options › Ableton Link.
u.0.1.28.n4: Freeze and Bounce (Clip-launch workflow): Live's Freeze Track with the track's effects, Bounce Track in Place, Bounce to New Track and Consolidate.
u.0.1.28.n5: Clip envelopes: volume and pan lines on audio clips, in the FL layout's clip menu and in the Clip View's Envelopes tab, written to .flp as FL's own automation and to .als as Live's clip envelopes.
u.0.1.28.n6: Drag samples onto plugins: a sample dragged from the Browser onto a plugin's own window reaches the plugin, as a drop from your file manager does, and an instrument dropped on a Playlist track header makes it an instrument track. (#174, #152)
u.0.1.28.n7: Live sets (.als): Hybrid Reverb, Roar and Grain Delay convert, Live's device and rack presets drop onto a mixer slot, grooves come in and go back, and Drum Buss opens on Anvil Bus, LYNX SHARE's new drum-bus effect fitted to Live's renders.
u.0.1.28.n8: FL Studio Mobile (.flm): Settings › Files › FL Studio Mobile resources points LYNX SHARE at your own copy of the app's Resources folder, and kits, DW Sampler programs, SoundFonts and the Slicer play their factory sounds. FL projects with the FL Studio Mobile Rack play it too.
u.0.1.28.n9: Simple workflow: a 16-pad Sampler track you play with the computer keys, a folder of stems and MIDI (such as BandLab's Download Stems) in one drop, and Export this track.
u.0.1.28.n10: Remote Control API (experimental, off by default), contributed by guike8: a program on the same computer can read and edit the open project.
u.0.1.28.b0: Playlist track headers, as in FL Studio: resize a track by dragging the bottom of its header (#164), Ctrl+click adds tracks and inserts to the selection (#163), and an option links Playlist tracks to mixer tracks with volume and pan on the headers (#170).
u.0.1.28.b1: Stop and Space go back to the last place you clicked on the ruler (Remember seek time, on by default as in FL Studio). (#169)
u.0.1.28.b2: Pick a clip that is already in the Playlist for the Pencil and the Brush, hide the Picker panel, and size the windows of LYNX SHARE's own plugins with a Scaling menu. (#175, #152)
u.0.1.28.b3: The Piano roll's event editor can be resized by dragging the bar above it, as in FL Studio.
u.0.1.28.b4: Slicex: slide notes bend slices as in FL Studio, and the editor has FL's display modes, Freeze and Slide buttons and LFO flags. (#172, #157)
u.0.1.28.b5: Save preset in the preset box of the built-in instruments, and FL Studio's own FL Studio VSTi plugin now loads (#162).
u.0.1.28.b6: After a plugin crash one click runs that plugin in a separate process from then on. On Linux and macOS the crash guard also covers plugin editors, presets and plugins' own threads, and dropouts are counted with their cause.
u.0.1.28.b7: Effects closer to the originals: Ember Saturator's Tape style gets a measured tape model with tape speeds, and the Compressor, Glow Leveler and Spiral Echo scored higher against the plugins they stand in for.
u.0.1.28.b8: Go back to the previous version from the Help menu, Test audio output in the Help menu and the setup wizard, and MIDI devices that can be plugged in and out while LYNX SHARE runs.
u.0.1.28.f0: A slide note on the same step as its note did not bend it, and on Linux plugin windows did not close cleanly, had no border and took no typing. (#165)
u.0.1.28.f1: Opening a project with missing files crashed at an interface size above 100 %. (#165)
u.0.1.28.f2: Projects saved by the FL Studio trial opened with scrambled tempo, channels and routing. (#171)
u.0.1.28.f3: LYNX SHARE's own plugins could not be loaded by other hosts on Linux in 0.1.27.
u.0.1.28.f4: A 6/8 song or scene played a three-beat bar.
u.0.1.28.f5: Exports with automation depended on the buffer size, and inserts fed only by a plugin's extra outputs got no stem.
u.0.1.28.k0: With render-ahead, edits to the part rendered ahead are heard up to 23 ms late. It can be turned off in Options › Audio settings.
u.0.1.28.k1: Dropping a sample into a plugin was tried on Linux only; on Windows and macOS the full drop has not been tested by hand yet. (#174)
u.0.1.28.k2: A track that plays Session clips cannot be track-frozen yet, and some of Live's devices (the Spectral devices, Amp, Cabinet, Vinyl, FM Operator patches) are still dropped on import.
